title: Hypergraphs
summary: Edges with any number of vertices. Turán and Ramsey questions become much harder: the Turán density of the $3$-uniform $K_4^{(3)}$ is still unknown.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #563
research_problems.statement:
Let $F(n,\alpha)$ denote the smallest $m$ such that there exists a $2$-colouring of the edges of
$K_n$ so that every $X\subseteq [n]$ with $\lvert X\rvert\geq m$ contains more than
$\alpha \binom{\lvert X\rvert}{2}$ many edges of each colour.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #716
research_problems.statement:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the family of all $3$-uniform hypergraphs with $6$ vertices and $3$ $3$-edges.
Is it true that
$$\mathrm{ex}_3(n,\mathcal{F})=o(n^2)?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1020
research_problems.statement: Let $f(n;r,k)$ be the maximal number of edges in an $r$-uniform hypergraph which contains no set of $k$ many independent edges.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #835
research_problems.statement:
Does there exist a $k>2$ such that the $k$-sized subsets of {1,...,2k} can be coloured with
$k+1$ colours such that for every $A\subset \{1,\ldots,2k\}$ with $\lvert A\rvert=k+1$ all $k+1$
colours appear among the $k$-sized subsets of $A$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #834
research_problems.statement:
(a) Does there exist a $3$-critical $3$-uniform hypergraph in which every vertex has degree
$\geq 7$, where criticality means that the transversal number is $3$ and deleting any edge
reduces it to $2$?

(b) Does there exist a $3$-critical $3$-uniform hypergraph with minimum degree at least $7$,
where criticality means that deleting any edge or vertex reduces chromatic number $3$ to $2$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #775
research_problems.statement:
Is there a $3$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices which contains at least $n-O(1)$ different
sizes of cliques (maximal complete subgraphs)?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #643
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $f(n;t)$ be minimal such that if a $t$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices contains at least
$f(n;t)$ edges then there must be four edges $A,B,C,D$ such that
$$A\cup B= C\cup D$$
and
$$A\cap B=C\cap D=\emptyset.$$
Estimate $f(n;t)$ - in particular, is it true that for $t\geq 3$
$$f(n;t)=(1+o(1))\binom{n}{t-1}?$$

(b) Is it true that $f(n;t)=(1+o(1))\binom{n}{t-1}$ for $t\geq 3$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #562
research_problems.statement:
Let $R_r(n)$ denote the $r$-uniform hypergraph Ramsey number: the minimal $m$ such that if we
$2$-colour all edges of the complete $r$-uniform hypergraph on $m$ vertices then there must be some
monochromatic copy of the complete $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #832
research_problems.statement:
Let $r\geq 3$ and $k$ be sufficiently large in terms of $r$. Is it true that every $r$-uniform
hypergraph with chromatic number $k$ has at least
$$\binom{(r-1)(k-1)+1}{r}$$
edges, with equality only for the complete graph on $(r-1)(k-1)+1$ vertices?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #712
research_problems.statement:
Determine, for any $k>r>2$, the limiting value as $n\to\infty$ of
$$\frac{\mathrm{ex}_r(n,K_k^r)}{\binom{n}{r}},$$
where $\mathrm{ex}_r(n,K_k^r)$ is the largest number of $r$-edges which can placed on $n$ vertices
so that there exists no set of $k$ vertices which is covered by all $\binom{k}{r}$ possible
$r$-edges.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #593
research_problems.statement:
Characterize those finite 3-uniform hypergraphs which appear
in every 3-uniform hypergraph of chromatic number $> \aleph_0$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #747
research_problems.statement:
How large should $\ell(n)$ be such that, almost surely, a random $3$-uniform hypergraph on $3n$
vertices with $\ell(n)$ edges must contain $n$ vertex-disjoint edges?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #161
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $\alpha\in[0,1/2)$ and $n,t\geq 1$. Let $F^{(t)}(n,\alpha)$ be the smallest $m$ such that we can
$2$-colour the edges of the complete $t$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices such that if $X\subseteq
[n]$ with $\lvert X\rvert \geq m$ then there are at least $\alpha \binom{\lvert X\rvert}{t}$ many
$t$-subsets of $X$ of each colour. For fixed $n,t$ as we change $\alpha$ from $0$ to $1/2$ does
$F^{(t)}(n,\alpha)$ increase continuously or are there jumps? Only one jump?

(b) For fixed $t\geq 3$, do all positive densities below $1/2$ give the same asymptotic order?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #794
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that every $3$-uniform hypergraph on $3n$ vertices with at least $n^3+1$ edges must
contain either a subgraph on $4$ vertices with $3$ edges or a subgraph on $5$ vertices with $7$
edges?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1158
research_problems.statement:
Let $K_{t}(r)$ be the complete $t$-partite $t$-uniform hypergraph with $r$ vertices in each class.
Is it true that
$$\mathrm{ex}_t(n,K_t(r)) \geq n^{t-r^{1-t}-o(1)}$$
for all $t,r\geq 2$? The restriction $r\geq 2$ excludes forbidding a single edge.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1128
research_problems.statement: (disproved by Prikry–Mills, 1978):

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #836
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $r\geq 2$ and let $G$ be an intersecting $r$-uniform hypergraph with chromatic number
$3$. Must $G$ contain $O(r^2)$ many vertices? Vertices are counted in the union of the edges,
so isolated vertices are excluded.

(b) In an intersecting $r$-uniform hypergraph with chromatic number $3$, must there be two
distinct edges which meet in $\gg r$ many vertices?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #500
research_problems.statement:
What is $\mathrm{ex}_3(n,K_4^3)$? That is, the largest number of $3$-edges which can placed on $n$
vertices so that there exists no $K_4^3$, a set of 4 vertices which is covered by all 4 possible
$3$-edges.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #780
research_problems.statement:
Suppose $n\geq kr+(t-1)(k-1)$ and the edges of the complete $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$
vertices are $t$-coloured. Prove that some colour class must contain $k$ pairwise disjoint edges.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #901
research_problems.statement:
Let $m(n)$ be minimal such that there is an $n$-uniform hypergraph with $m(n)$ edges which is
$3$-chromatic. Estimate $m(n)$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #207
research_problems.statement:
For any $g\geq 2$, if $n$ is sufficiently large and $\equiv 1,3\pmod{6}$ then there exists a
3-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices such that

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #564
research_problems.statement:
Let $R_3(n)$ be the minimal $m$ such that if the edges of the $3$-uniform hypergraph on $m$
vertices are $2$-coloured then there is a monochromatic copy of the complete $3$-uniform
hypergraph on $n$ vertices.

Is there some constant $c>0$ such that
$$ R_3(n) \geq 2^{2^{cn}}? $$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1024
research_problems.statement:
Let $f(n)$ be such that every $3$-uniform linear hypergraph on $n$ vertices contains an independent
set on $f(n)$ vertices. Estimate $f(n)$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #833
research_problems.statement:
Does there exist an absolute constant $c>0$ such that, for all $r\geq 2$, in any $r$-uniform
hypergraph with chromatic number $3$ there is a vertex contained in at least $(1+c)^r$ many edges?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1177
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $G$ be a finite $3$-uniform hypergraph, and let $F_G(\kappa)$ denote the collection of
$3$-uniform hypergraphs with chromatic number $\kappa$ not containing $G$. If $F_G(\aleph_1)$ is not
empty then there exists $X\in F_G(\aleph_1)$ of cardinality at most $2^{2^{\aleph_0}}$. If both
$F_G(\aleph_1)$ and $F_H(\aleph_1)$ are non-empty then $F_G(\aleph_1)\cap F_H(\aleph_1)$ is
non-empty. If $\kappa,\lambda$ are uncountable cardinals and $F_G(\kappa)$ is non-empty then
$F_G(\lambda)$ is non-empty.

(b) If both $F_G(\aleph_1)$ and $F_H(\aleph_1)$ are non-empty then
$F_G(\aleph_1)\cap F_H(\al

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #837
research_problems.statement:
Let $k\geq 2$ and $A_k\subseteq [0,1]$ be the set of $\alpha$ such that there exists some
$\beta(\alpha)>\alpha$ with the property that, if $G_1,G_2,\ldots$ is a sequence of $k$-uniform
hypergraphs with
$$\liminf \frac{e(G_n)}{\binom{\lvert G_n\rvert}{k}} >\alpha$$
then there exist subgraphs $H_n\subseteq G_n$ such that $\lvert H_n\rvert \to \infty$ and
$$\liminf \frac{e(H_n)}{\binom{\lvert H_n\rvert}{k}} >\beta,$$
and further that this property does not necessarily hold if $>\alpha$ is replaced by $\geq \alpha$.
What is $A_3$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #719
research_problems.statement:
Let $r\geq 2$, and let $\mathrm{ex}_r(n;K_{r+1}^r)$ be the maximum number of $r$-edges that can
be placed on $n$ vertices without forming a $K_{r+1}^r$ (the $r$-uniform complete graph on
$r+1$ vertices). Is every
$r$-hypergraph $G$ on $n$ vertices the union of at most $\mathrm{ex}_{r}(n;K_{r+1}^r)$ many copies
of $K_r^r$ and $K_{r+1}^r$, no two of which share a $K_r^r$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1178
research_problems.statement:
For $r\geq 3$ let $d_r(e)$ be the minimal $d$ such that
$$\mathrm{ex}_r(n,\mathcal{F})=o(n^2),$$
where $\mathcal{F}$ is the family of $r$-uniform hypergraphs on $d$ vertices with $e$ edges. Prove
that
$$d_r(e)=(r-2)e+3$$
for all $r,e\geq 3$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1022
research_problems.statement:
Is there a constant $c_t$, where $c_t\to \infty$ as $t\to \infty$, such that if $\mathcal{F}$
is a finite family of finite sets, all of size at least $t$, and for every set $X$ there are
$<c_t\lvert X\rvert$ many $A\in \mathcal{F}$ with $A\subseteq X$, then $\mathcal{F}$ has
chromatic number $2$ (in other words, has property B)?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1157
research_problems.statement:
Let $s,k,r\geq 2$. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the family of all $r$-uniform hypergraphs with $k$ vertices
and $s$ edges. Determine
$$\mathrm{ex}_r(n,\mathcal{F}).$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1075
research_problems.statement:
Let $r\geq 3$. There exists $c_r>r^{-r}$ such that, for any $\epsilon>0$, if $n$ is sufficiently
large, the following holds. Any $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices with at least
$(1+\epsilon)(n/r)^r$ many edges contains a subgraph on $m$ vertices with at least $c_rm^r$ edges,
where $m=m(n)\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$.

title: Extremal graph theory
summary: How many edges can a graph on $n$ vertices have without containing a fixed subgraph $H$? Turán answers it for cliques; Erdős–Stone for all non-bipartite $H$; bipartite $H$ remain largely open.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #147
research_problems.statement:
If $H$ is bipartite with minimum degree $r$ then there exists $\epsilon=\epsilon(H)>0$ such that
$$\mathrm{ex}(n;H) \gg n^{2-\frac{1}{r-1}+\epsilon}.$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #713
research_problems.statement:
(a) Is it true that, for every bipartite graph $G$, there exists some $\alpha\in [1,2)$ and $c>0$ such that $$\mathrm{ex}(n;G)\sim cn^\alpha?$$

(b) Must $\alpha$ be rational?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1079
research_problems.statement:
Let $r\geq 4$. If $G$ is a graph on $n$ vertices with at least $\mathrm{ex}(n;K_r)$ edges then
must $G$ contain a vertex with degree $d\gg_r n$ whose neighbourhood contains at least
$\mathrm{ex}(d;K_{r-1})$ edges?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #579
research_problems.statement:
Let $\delta > 0$. If $n$ is sufficiently large and $G$ is a graph on $n$ vertices with no
$K_{2,2,2}$ (the octahedron) and at least $\delta n^2$ edges, must $G$ contain an independent
set of size $\gg_\delta n$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #146
research_problems.statement:
If $H$ is bipartite and is $r$-degenerate, that is, every induced subgraph of $H$ has minimum
degree $\leq r$, then
$$\mathrm{ex}(n;H) \ll n^{2-1/r}.$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #766
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $f(n;k,l)=\min \mathrm{ex}(n;G)$, where $G$ ranges over all graphs with $k$ vertices and $l$
edges.

(b) For fixed $k$ and large $n$ is $f(n;k,l)$ a strictly monotone function of $l$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #712
research_problems.statement:
Determine, for any $k>r>2$, the limiting value as $n\to\infty$ of
$$\frac{\mathrm{ex}_r(n,K_k^r)}{\binom{n}{r}},$$
where $\mathrm{ex}_r(n,K_k^r)$ is the largest number of $r$-edges which can placed on $n$ vertices
so that there exists no set of $k$ vertices which is covered by all $\binom{k}{r}$ possible
$r$-edges.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #714
research_problems.statement: Is it true that $$\mathrm{ex}(n; K_{r,r}) \gg n^{2-1/r}?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #572
research_problems.statement:
Show that for $k\geq 3$
$$\mathrm{ex}(n;C_{2k})\gg n^{1+\frac{1}{k}}.$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #180
research_problems.statement:
If $\mathcal{F}$ is a finite set of finite graphs then $\mathrm{ex}(n;\mathcal{F})$ is the maximum
number of edges a graph on $n$ vertices can have without containing any subgraphs from
$\mathcal{F}$. Note that it is trivial that $\mathrm{ex}(n;\mathcal{F})\leq \mathrm{ex}(n;G)$ for
every $G\in\mathcal{F}$. Is it true that, for every $\mathcal{F}$, there exists $G\in\mathcal{F}$
such that
$$\mathrm{ex}(n;G)\ll_{\mathcal{F}}\mathrm{ex}(n;\mathcal{F})?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #767
research_problems.statement:
Let $g_k(n)$ be the maximal number of edges possible on a graph with $n$ vertices which does not
contain a cycle with $k$ chords incident to a vertex on the cycle. Is it true that
$$g_k(n)=(k+1)n-(k+1)^2$$
for $n$ sufficiently large?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #794
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that every $3$-uniform hypergraph on $3n$ vertices with at least $n^3+1$ edges must
contain either a subgraph on $4$ vertices with $3$ edges or a subgraph on $5$ vertices with $7$
edges?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #113
research_problems.statement:
If $G$ is bipartite then $\mathrm{ex}(n;G)\ll n^{3/2}$ if and only $G$ is $2$-degenerate, that
is, $G$ contains no induced subgraph with minimal degree at least 3.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1158
research_problems.statement:
Let $K_{t}(r)$ be the complete $t$-partite $t$-uniform hypergraph with $r$ vertices in each class.
Is it true that
$$\mathrm{ex}_t(n,K_t(r)) \geq n^{t-r^{1-t}-o(1)}$$
for all $t,r\geq 2$? The restriction $r\geq 2$ excludes forbidding a single edge.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #500
research_problems.statement:
What is $\mathrm{ex}_3(n,K_4^3)$? That is, the largest number of $3$-edges which can placed on $n$
vertices so that there exists no $K_4^3$, a set of 4 vertices which is covered by all 4 possible
$3$-edges.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #59
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that the number of graphs on $n$ vertices which do not contain $G$ is
$$\leq 2^{(1+o(1))\mathrm{ex}(n;G)}?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #571
research_problems.statement: Show that for any rational $\alpha \in [1,2)$ there exists a bipartite graph $G$ such that $$\mathrm{ex}(n;G)\asymp n^{\alpha}.$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1157
research_problems.statement:
Let $s,k,r\geq 2$. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the family of all $r$-uniform hypergraphs with $k$ vertices
and $s$ edges. Determine
$$\mathrm{ex}_r(n,\mathcal{F}).$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #573
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that
$$\mathrm{ex}(n;\{C_3,C_4\})\sim (n/2)^{3/2}?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #765
research_problems.statement: Give an asymptotic formula for $\mathrm{ex}(n; C_4)$.

title: Ramsey theory
summary: Every $2$-colouring of the edges of a large complete graph contains a monochromatic $K_k$. The Ramsey number $R(k)$ is the threshold; $\sqrt2^{\,k} \le R(k) \le 4^k$, improved to $(4-\varepsilon)^k$ in 2023.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #596
research_problems.statement:
(Erdős–Hajnal, [Er87]). For which graph pairs $(G_1, G_2)$ is it
true that

(1) for every $n \geq 1$ there is a graph $H$ without a $G_1$ such that any
      $n$-colouring of $H$'s edges contains a monochromatic $G_2$, and yet
  (2) for every graph $H$ without a $G_1$ there is an $\aleph_0$-colouring of $H$'s edges
      with no monochromatic $G_2$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #563
research_problems.statement:
Let $F(n,\alpha)$ denote the smallest $m$ such that there exists a $2$-colouring of the edges of
$K_n$ so that every $X\subseteq [n]$ with $\lvert X\rvert\geq m$ contains more than
$\alpha \binom{\lvert X\rvert}{2}$ many edges of each colour.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1105
research_problems.statement:
(a) The anti-Ramsey number $\mathrm{AR}(n,G)$ is the maximum possible number of colours in which the
edges of $K_n$ can be coloured without creating a rainbow copy of $G$ (i.e. one in which all edges
have different colours).

Let $C_k$ be the cycle on $k$ vertices. Is it true that
$\mathrm{AR}(n,C_k)=\left(\frac{k-2}{2}+\frac{1}{k-1}\right)n+O(1)$?

(b) Let $P_k$ be the path on $k$ vertices and $\ell=\lfloor\frac{k-1}{2}\rfloor$. If $n\geq k\geq 5$
then is $\mathrm{AR}(n,P_k)$ equal to $\max\left(\binom{k-2}{2}+1,
\binom{\ell-1}{2}+(\ell-1)(n-\ell+1)+\epsilon\right)$where $\epsilon=1$ if $k$ i

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #78
research_problems.statement:
Let $R(k)$ be the Ramsey number for $K_k$. Give a constructive proof that $R(k) > C^k$ for some
constant $C > 1$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1176
research_problems.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$. Is it true that there is a colouring of the
edges with $\aleph_1$ many colours such that, in any countable colouring of the vertices, there
exists a vertex colour containing all edge colours?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #551
research_problems.statement:
Prove that
$$R(C_k,K_n)=(k-1)(n-1)+1$$
for $k\geq n\geq 3$ (except when $n=k=3$).

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #549
research_problems.statement:
If $T$ is a tree which is a bipartite graph with $k$ vertices in one class and $2k$ vertices
in the other class then
$$R(T)=4k-1.$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1199
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that in any 2-colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ there exists an infinite set $A$
such that all elements of $A+A$ are the same colour?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #163
research_problems.statement:
The Burr-Erdős conjecture: For any $d\geq 1$ if $H$ is a graph such that every subgraph
contains a vertex of degree at most $d$ then
$$R(H)\ll_d n.$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #172
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that in any finite colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ there exist arbitrarily large finite $A$ such that all sums
and products of distinct elements in $A$ are the same colour?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1219
research_problems.statement:
Let $(n_k)$ be an increasing sequence of integers such that $2^{\aleph_{n_k}}$ is strictly
increasing, and $2^{\aleph_{n_0}} > \aleph_\omega$. Is it true that
$$\sum_k 2^{\aleph_{n_k}} \to (\aleph_\omega)^2?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #214
research_problems.statement:
Let $S\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be such that no two points in $S$ are distance $1$ apart. Must the
complement of $S$ contain four points which form a unit square?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #183
research_problems.statement:
Let $R(3;k)$ be the minimal $n$ such that if the edges of $K_n$ are coloured with $k$ colours
then there must exist a monochromatic triangle. Determine
$$\lim_{k\to \infty}R(3;k)^{1/k}.$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #720
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $\hat{R}(G)$ denote the size Ramsey number, the minimal number of edges $m$ such that there
is a graph $H$ with $m$ edges such that in any $2$-colouring of the edges of $H$ there is a
monochromatic copy of $G$.

Is it true that, if $P_n$ is the path of length $n$, then $\hat{R}(P_n)/n\to \infty$?

(b) Is it true that, if $P_n$ is the path of length $n$, then $\hat{R}(P_n)/n^2 \to 0$?

(c) Is it true that, if $C_n$ is the cycle with $n$ edges, then $\hat{R}(C_n) =o(n^2)$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #598
research_problems.statement:
Let $\kappa = (2^{\aleph_0})^+$. This is the successor cardinal of the continuum.

**Erdős Problem 598:**
Let $m$ be an infinite cardinal and $\kappa$ be the successor cardinal of $2^{\aleph_0}$.
Can one colour the countable subsets of $m$ using $\kappa$ many colours so that every
$X \subseteq m$ with $|X| = \kappa$ contains subsets of all possible colours?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #615
research_problems.statement:
Does there exist some constant $c > 0$ such that for all sufficiently large $n$, if $G$ is a
graph with $n$ vertices and at least $(1/8 - c)n^2$ edges then $G$ must contain either a $K_4$
or an independent set on at least $n/\log n$ vertices?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #569
research_problems.statement:
Let $k\geq 1$. What is the best possible $c_k$ such that
$$R(C_{2k+1},H)\leq c_k m$$
for any graph $H$ on $m$ edges without isolated vertices?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #570
research_problems.statement:
Let $k\geq 3$. Is it true that, if $m$ is sufficiently large, for any graph $H$ on $m$ edges
without isolated vertices,
$$R(C_k,H) \leq 2m+\left\lfloor\frac{k-1}{2}\right\rfloor?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1030
research_problems.statement:
Let $R(k,l)$ be the usual Ramsey number: the smallest $n$ such that if the edges of $K_n$ are
coloured red and blue then there exists either a red $K_k$ or a blue $K_l$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #189
research_problems.statement:
If $\mathbb{R}^2$ is finitely coloured then must there exist some colour class which contains the
vertices of a rectangle of every area?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #562
research_problems.statement:
Let $R_r(n)$ denote the $r$-uniform hypergraph Ramsey number: the minimal $m$ such that if we
$2$-colour all edges of the complete $r$-uniform hypergraph on $m$ vertices then there must be some
monochromatic copy of the complete $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #544
research_problems.statement:
(a) Show that
$$R(3,k+1)-R(3,k)\to\infty$$
as $k\to \infty$.

(b) Similarly, prove or disprove that
$$R(3,k+1)-R(3,k)=o(k).$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #965
research_problems.statement:
Erdős asks in [Er75b] if for every 2-coloring of ℝ, there is an uncountable set $A ⊆ ℝ$ such that
all sums $a + b$ for $a, b ∈ A, a ≠ b$ have the same colour.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #639
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that if the edges of $K_n$ are 2-coloured then there are at most $n^2/4$ many edges
which do not occur in a monochromatic triangle?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #159
research_problems.statement:
There exists some constant $c>0$ such that
$$R(C_4,K_n) \ll n^{2-c}.$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #667
research_problems.statement:
Let $p, q \geq 1$ be fixed integers. Define $H(n) = H(n; p, q)$ to be the largest $m$ such that any
graph on $n$ vertices where every set of $p$ vertices spans at least $q$ edges must contain a
complete graph on $m$ vertices. Is
$$ c(p, q) = \liminf_{n \to \infty} \frac{\log H(n)}{\log n} $$
a strictly increasing function of $q$ for $1 \leq q \leq \binom{p-1}{2} + 1$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #552
research_problems.statement:
(a) Determine the Ramsey number
$$R(C_4, S_n),$$
where $S_n=K_{1,n}$ is the star on $n+1$ vertices.

(b) In particular, is it true that, for any $c > 0$, there are infinitely many $n$ such that
$$R(C_4, S_n) \leq n + \sqrt{n} - c?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #949
research_problems.statement:
Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be a set containing no solutions to $a + b = c$.
Must there be a set $A \subseteq \mathbb{R} \setminus S$ of cardinality continuum such that
$A + A \subseteq \mathbb{R}\setminus S$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #592
research_problems.statement:
Determine which countable ordinals $β$ have the property that, if $α = \omega^β$, then in any
red/blue colouring of the edges of $K_α$ there is either a red $K_α$ or a blue $K_3$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #165
research_problems.statement: Give an asymptotic formula for $R(3,k)$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #566
research_problems.statement:
Let $G$ be such that any subgraph on $k$ vertices has at most $2k-3$ edges.
Is it true that, if $H$ has $m$ edges and no isolated vertices, then $R(G,H) \ll m$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #161
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $\alpha\in[0,1/2)$ and $n,t\geq 1$. Let $F^{(t)}(n,\alpha)$ be the smallest $m$ such that we can
$2$-colour the edges of the complete $t$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices such that if $X\subseteq
[n]$ with $\lvert X\rvert \geq m$ then there are at least $\alpha \binom{\lvert X\rvert}{t}$ many
$t$-subsets of $X$ of each colour. For fixed $n,t$ as we change $\alpha$ from $0$ to $1/2$ does
$F^{(t)}(n,\alpha)$ increase continuously or are there jumps? Only one jump?

(b) For fixed $t\geq 3$, do all positive densities below $1/2$ give the same asymptotic order?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #545
research_problems.statement:
Let $m$ be sufficiently large and let $G$ be a graph with $m$ edges and no isolated vertices.
Is the Ramsey number $R(G)$ maximised when $G$ is 'as complete as possible'?
That is, if $m=\binom{n}{2}+t$ edges with $0\leq t < n$
then is
$$R(G)\leq R(H),$$
where $H$ is the graph formed by connecting a new vertex to $t$ of the vertices of $K_n$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #162
research_problems.statement:
Let $\alpha > 0$ and $n \geq 1$. Let $F(n,\alpha)$ be the largest $k$ such that there exists some
2-colouring of the edges of $K_n$ in which any induced subgraph $H$ on at least $k$ vertices
contains more than $\alpha\binom{|H|}{2}$ many edges of each colour.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #555
research_problems.statement:
Let $R_k(G)$ be the least $m$ such that every $k$-colouring of the edges of $K_m$ contains a
monochromatic copy of $G$. Determine $R_k(C_{2n})$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #70
research_problems.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{c}$ be the order type of the real numbers,
let $\beta$ be a countable ordinal, and let $2 \le n < \omega$.
Is it true that $\mathfrak{c} \to (\beta, n)^3_2$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #801
research_problems.statement:
If $G$ is a graph on $n$ vertices containing no independent set on $>n^{1/2}$ vertices then there
is a set of $\leq n^{1/2}$ vertices containing $\gg n^{1/2}\log n$ edges.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #77
research_problems.statement:
If $R(k)$ is the Ramsey number for $K_k$, the minimal $n$ such that every $2$-colouring of the edges
of $K_n$ contains a monochromatic copy of $K_k$, then find the value of
$$\lim_{k\to \infty}R(k)^{1/k}.$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #986
research_problems.statement:
For any fixed $s\geq 3$,
$$R(s,k) \gg \frac{k^{s-1}}{(\log k)^c}$$
for some constant $c=c(s)>0$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #188
research_problems.statement:
What is the smallest $k$ such that $\mathbb{R}^2$ can be red/blue coloured with no pair of red
points unit distance apart, and no $k$-term arithmetic progression of blue points with distance 1?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #800
research_problems.statement:
If $G$ is a graph on $n$ vertices which has no two adjacent vertices of degree $\geq 3$ then
$$R(G)\ll n,$$
where the implied constant is absolute.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #568
research_problems.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph such that $R(G,T_n)\ll n$ for any tree $T_n$ on $n$ vertices and
$R(G,K_n)\ll n^2$. Is it true that, for any $H$ with $m$ edges and no isolated vertices,
$$R(G,H)\ll m?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #911
research_problems.statement:
Let $\hat{R}(G)$ denote the size Ramsey number, the minimal number of edges $m$ such that there is
a graph $H$ with $m$ edges that is Ramsey for $G$.

Is there a function $f$ such that $f(x)/x\to \infty$ as $x\to \infty$ such that, for all large $C$,
if $G$ is a graph with $n$ vertices and $e\geq Cn$ edges then
$$\hat{R}(G) > f(C) e?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #590
research_problems.statement:
Let $α$ be the infinite ordinal $\omega^{\omega}$. It was proved by Chang [Ch72] that any red/blue
colouring of the edges of $K_α$ there is either a red $K_α$ or a blue $K_3$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #613
research_problems.statement:
Let $n \geq 3$ and $G$ be a graph with $\binom{2n+1}{2} - \binom{n}{2} - 1$ edges.
Must $G$ be the union of a bipartite graph and a graph with maximum degree less than $n$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #556
research_problems.statement:
Erdős Problem 556 (Bondy–Erdős): for all $n \ge 4$,
$$R(C_n; 3) \le 4n - 3.$$
The case $n = 3$ is excluded since $R(K_3; 3) = 17$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #636
research_problems.statement:
Suppose $G$ is a graph on $n$ vertices which contains no complete graph or independent set on
$\gg \log n$ many vertices. Must $G$ contain $\gg n^{5/2}$ induced subgraphs which pairwise differ
in either the number of vertices or the number of edges?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1090
research_problems.statement: Let $k\geq 3$. Does there exist a finite set $A\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ such that, in any $2$-colouring of $A$, there exists a line which contains at least $k$ points from $A$, and all the points of $A$ on the line have the same colour?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #85
research_problems.statement:
Let $f(n)$ be the smallest integer for which every graph on $n$ vertices with minimal degree $\geq
f(n)$ contains a $C_4$.

Is it true that, for all large $n$, $f(n + 1) \ge f(n)$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #80
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $c>0$ and let $f_c(n)$ be the maximal $m$ such that every graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and
at least $cn^2$ edges, where each edge is contained in at least one triangle, must contain a
book of size $m$, that is, an edge shared by at least $m$ different triangles. Estimate
$f_c(n)$. In particular, is it true that $f_c(n)>n^\epsilon$ for some $\epsilon>0$?

(b) The weaker question from the same problem: is $f_c(n) \gg \log n$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1128
research_problems.statement: (disproved by Prikry–Mills, 1978):

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #547
research_problems.statement:
If $T$ is a tree on $n$ vertices then
$$R(T) \leq 2n-2.$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #812
research_problems.statement:
(a) Is it true that $\frac{R(n+1)}{R(n)}\geq 1+c$ for some constant $c>0$, for all large $n$?

(b) Is it true that $R(n+1)-R(n) \gg n^2$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #557
research_problems.statement:
Let $R_k(G)$ denote the minimal $m$ such that if the edges of $K_m$ are $k$-coloured then there
is a monochromatic copy of $G$. Is it true that
$$R_k(T)\leq kn+O(1)$$
for any tree $T$ on $n$ vertices?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #546
research_problems.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with no isolated vertices and $m$ edges. Is it true that
$$R(G) \leq 2^{O(m^{1/2})}?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #550
research_problems.statement:
Let $m_1\leq\cdots\leq m_k$ and $n$ be sufficiently large. If $T$ is a tree on $n$ vertices
and $G$ is the complete multipartite graph with vertex class sizes $m_1,\ldots,m_k$ then prove that
$$R(T,G)\leq (\chi(G)-1)(R(T,K_{m_1,m_2})-1)+m_1.$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1029
research_problems.statement:
If $R(k)$ is the Ramsey number for $K_k$, the minimal $n$ such that every $2$-colouring of the edges
of $K_n$ contains a monochromatic copy of $K_k$, then
$$\frac{R(k)}{k2^{k/2}}\to \infty.$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #564
research_problems.statement:
Let $R_3(n)$ be the minimal $m$ such that if the edges of the $3$-uniform hypergraph on $m$
vertices are $2$-coloured then there is a monochromatic copy of the complete $3$-uniform
hypergraph on $n$ vertices.

Is there some constant $c>0$ such that
$$ R_3(n) \geq 2^{2^{cn}}? $$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #181
research_problems.statement:
Let $Q_n$ be the $n$-dimensional hypercube graph (so that $Q_n$ has $2^n$ vertices and
$n2^{n-1}$ edges). Prove that $$R(Q_n) \ll 2^n.$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #567
research_problems.statement:
(a) **Erdős Problem 567 (Q3)**

Is $Q_3$ (the 3-dimensional hypercube) Ramsey size linear?

(b) **Erdős Problem 567 (K33)**

Is $K_{3,3}$ Ramsey size linear?

(c) **Erdős Problem 567 (H5)**

Is $H_5$ ($C_5$ with two vertex-disjoint chords) Ramsey size linear?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #559
research_problems.statement:
Let $\hat{R}(G)$ denote the size Ramsey number, the minimal number of edges $m$ such that there is
a graph $H$ with $m$ edges that is Ramsey for $G$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1198
research_problems.statement:
If $\mathbb{N}$ is $2$-coloured, must there exist an infinite set $A=\{a_1<a_2<\cdots\}$ such that
all expressions of the shape
$$\sum_{j=1}^{k}\prod_{i\in S_j}a_i,$$
for $k\geq 1$ and pairwise disjoint nonempty finite sets of indices $S_1,\ldots,S_k$ (excluding the
trivial expressions $a_i$, that is $k=1$ and $|S_1|=1$), have the same colour?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #561
research_problems.statement:
Let $\hat{R}(G)$ denote the size Ramsey number, the minimal number of edges $m$ such that there
is a graph $H$ with $m$ edges such that in any $2$-colouring of the edges of $H$ there is a
monochromatic copy of $G$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #174
research_problems.statement:
A finite set $A\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ is called Ramsey if, for any $k\geq 1$, there exists some
$d=d(A,k)$ such that in any $k$-colouring of $\mathbb{R}^d$ there exists a monochromatic copy
of $A$. Characterise the Ramsey sets in $\mathbb{R}^n$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #560
research_problems.statement:
Let $\hat{R}(G)$ denote the size Ramsey number, the minimal number of edges $m$ such that there
is a graph $H$ with $m$ edges such that in any $2$-colouring of the edges of $H$ there is a
monochromatic copy of $G$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #79
research_problems.statement:
We say $G$ is Ramsey size linear if $R(G,H)\ll m$ for all graphs $H$ with $m$ edges and
no isolated vertices.

Are there infinitely many graphs $G$ which are not Ramsey size linear but such that all of
its proper subgraphs are?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #166
research_problems.statement:
Prove that
$$R(4,k) \gg \frac{k^3}{(\log k)^{O(1)}}.$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #88
research_problems.statement:
For any $\epsilon>0$ there exists $\delta=\delta(\epsilon)>0$ such that if $G$ is a graph on $n$
vertices with no independent set or clique of size $\geq \epsilon\log n$ then $G$ contains an
induced subgraph with $m$ edges for all $m\leq \delta n^2$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #173
research_problems.statement:
In any $2$-colouring of $\mathbb{R}^2$, for all but at most one triangle $T$ (up to
congruence), there is a monochromatic congruent copy of $T$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #591
research_problems.statement:
Let $α$ be the infinite ordinal $\omega^{\omega^2}$. Is it true that any red/blue colouring of the
edges of $K_α$ there is either a red $K_α$ or a blue $K_3$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #609
research_problems.statement:
Let $f(n)$ be the minimal $m$ such that if the edges of $K_{2^n+1}$ are coloured with $n$ colours
then there must be a monochromatic odd cycle of length at most $m$. Estimate $f(n)$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #87
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $0 < \epsilon < 1$. Is it true that, if $k$ is sufficiently large, then
$$R(G) > (1-\epsilon)^k R(k)$$
for every graph $G$ with chromatic number $\chi(G)=k$?

(b) Even stronger, is there some $c > 0$ such that, for all large $k$,
$$R(G) > c R(k)$$
for every graph $G$ with chromatic number $\chi(G)=k$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1174
research_problems.statement:
(a) **Erdős Problem 1174, part (i)** [Va99, 7.91]. A problem of Erdős and Hajnal:
does there exist a graph $G$ with no $K_4$ such that every edge colouring of $G$
with countably many colours contains a monochromatic $K_3$?

(b) **Erdős Problem 1174, part (ii)** [Va99, 7.91]. A problem of Erdős and Hajnal:
does there exist a graph $G$ with no $K_{\aleph_1}$ (that is, every clique of $G$
is countable) such that every edge colouring of $G$ with countably many colours
contains a monochromatic $K_{\aleph_0}$ (an infinite clique all of whose edges
receive the same colour)?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1167
research_problems.statement:
Let $r \geq 2$ be finite, $\gamma \geq 2$, and $\lambda$ be an infinite
cardinal. Let $\kappa_\alpha > r$ be cardinals for all $\alpha < \gamma$. Is it true
that
$$2^\lambda \to (\kappa_\alpha + 1)_{\alpha < \gamma}^{r+1}$$
implies
$$\lambda \to (\kappa_\alpha)_{\alpha < \gamma}^r?$$
Here $+$ means cardinal addition, so that $\kappa_\alpha + 1 = \kappa_\alpha$
if $\kappa_\alpha$ is infinite.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #582
research_problems.statement:
Does there exist a graph $G$ which contains no $K_4$, and yet any $2$-colouring of the edges
produces a monochromatic $K_3$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1014
research_problems.statement:
Let $R(k,l)$ be the Ramsey number, so the minimal $n$ such that every graph on at least $n$
vertices contains either a $K_k$ or an independent set on $l$ vertices.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #191
research_problems.statement:
Let $C>0$ be arbitrary. Is it true that, if $n$ is sufficiently large depending on $C$, then in
any $2$-colouring of $\binom{\{2,\ldots,n\}}{2}$ there exists some $X\subseteq \{2,\ldots,n\}$
such that $\binom{X}{2}$ is monochromatic and
$$\sum_{x\in X}\frac{1}{\log x}\geq C?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #554
research_problems.statement:
Let $R_k(G)$ denote the minimal $m$ such that if the edges of $K_m$ are $k$-coloured then there
is a monochromatic copy of $G$. Show that
$$\lim_{k\to \infty}\frac{R_k(C_{2n+1})}{R_k(K_3)}=0$$
for any $n\geq 2$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #810
research_problems.statement:
Does there exist some $\epsilon>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$, there exists a
graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with at least $\epsilon n^2$ edges whose edges can be coloured with $n$
colours so that every $C_4$ receives four distinct colours?
